Subject: Pilot scope & technical onramp — HeliosOps

Hi Sam (and team),

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate you walking through HeliosOps' immediate needs. Quick recap so we're aligned and to make the next steps explicit.

Summary of pain / goals we heard
- Production latency for real-time recommendations is spiking during peak windows (p90 ~ 1.7s), causing a measurable drop in conversions.
- Current infra is costly to scale for bursty traffic; you need predictable per-request economics.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII in prompt context, requirement for VPC or private tenancy and audit logs.

Proposed Pilot (90 days) — high level
- Scope: Inference integration for the recommendations endpoint only (GET /recommend), target 100 req/s with 50 concurrent sessions.
- Success metrics: p95 latency < 400ms for 95% of traffic; inference cost reduction >= 30% vs current baseline; no data exfiltration incidents.
- Deliverables: model variant selection, prompt set (starter suite of 150 prompts), integration runbook, telemetry dashboard with token-level cost.

Owners & timeline
- Redwood: Avery (you'll be my main point), Karthik (SE lead for infra integration), Priyom (pilot program manager).
- HeliosOps: Sam (product), Maya (platform), and your infra lead (TBD).
- Proposed kickoff: Week of July 6 (we can shift if procurement needs time).

Access & preliminary asks (attached checklist)
- Temporary service account with read-only access to the recommendations test cluster.
- Sample prompt logs (anonymized) and a small corpus to build prompt-evals.
- A CORS-enabled staging endpoint or a replay log for traffic simulation.

Attachments: HeliosOps-PoC-Scope-v1.pdf (scope + success criteria), access-checklist-helio.xlsx (technical access items).

Next steps
1) Confirm kickoff week (suggest July 6).
2) Maya or your infra lead to share the access owner and expected date we can provision the test account.
3) Karthik and I will share a pre-kickoff checklist and a lightweight integration guide by Friday (attached + link).

If anything above is off, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll treat this as what we agreed and start prepping the kickoff agenda.

Thanks,

Avery Johnson
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Avery — thanks for the clear write-up. This matches what I took away. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success metrics: we want p95 < 400ms under typical traffic shape and p95 <= 600ms under a 2x burst test. Can you confirm Redwood can simulate the burst profile?
- Data: we will provide anonymized prompt logs; full PII will not be included in the pilot. We do want the option to test with an encrypted key store (KMS) in a follow-up if pilot goes well.
- Timeline: July 6 kickoff works for product and me, but Maya is awaiting permission from our infra team to open the staging cluster for external access. She expects to confirm by EOD Thursday.

CC'ing Maya so she can chime in on the access timeline and add our infra lead if needed.

Sam

Hi Sam / Maya / Avery — quick technical note to make the onramp smoother. I worked up a short checklist and timeline below. Kicking this off ASAP will make the July 6 target realistic.

Pre-kickoff technical checklist (owner in parentheses)
- Staging endpoint or replay log available (HeliosOps infra) — required for us to warm KV caches and baseline latency.
- Service account + IP allowlist (HeliosOps infra) — temporary account with TLS + mTLS preferred.
- Sample prompt set (HeliosOps product) — 150 items, include 20 edge-case prompts for failure-mode checks.
- Telemetry ingestion (HeliosOps / Redwood) — set up a forwarding endpoint or S3 bucket where we can write token-level traces (redacted) for cost analysis.
- KMS integration note: Redwood supports customer-managed keys in Private deployments; for pilot we can encrypt logs at rest using our per-tenant key.

Pilot run plan (weeks)
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): access provisioning, baseline data transfer, Redwood integration smoke test.
- Week 1–2: model selection, prompt tuning, initial latency tuning (batching/caching config).
- Week 3–6: run simulated traffic and real traffic window; collect telemetry and run prompt-evals.
- Week 7–12: iterative optimization, handoff and runbook delivery, final acceptance tests.

Constraints & notes
- To meet p95 targets we will likely use a quantized variant and enable KV prefix caching for sessions longer than 8 tokens. We will share recommended model/quantization settings after we see the sample prompts.
- If staging access is blocked, we can run a replay from logs but it will add ~3 business days to the timeline.

I attached a one-page integration stub (I'll post to the shared drive momentarily). If you confirm who on HeliosOps can provision the service account and the expected date, we will lock the kickoff time and send a calendar invite with an internal tech agenda.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
